by: grants-1 session (Opus), step 6.3 (to be appended by the integrator at grants-1)
title: Grants from Gaming Machine Profits: the Department of Internal Affairs' national file of class 4 grants (CSV)
signals_note: Recognised by its header line alone: nineteen columns, Society_Name first, Region last. Measured on the file landed 21 October 2026 (a1da8259…, 37.7 MB): 178,739 records, every one 19 fields wide; 19 lines carry Windows-1252 bytes in a UTF-8 file; decisions dated 2021 to 2025; 47 society name forms.

tables.one record: one grant application a class 4 society decided (Accepted, Declined or Refunded), as the society reported it to the Department
tables.key: none published: the document's hash and the record's number (a built register's key)

notes: No purpose column: Category_1 and Category_2 are the Department's categories. Amount_Granted is 0 on a declined application and empty on 5,545 records. Organisation_NZBN and Organisation_Charities_Registration_Number are as the society reported them, mostly empty; an NZBN is kept only where it is 13 valid digits, a charity number only where it is CC and five or six digits (some are in spreadsheet exponent form). Date_of_Refund mixes NULL, empty and spreadsheet day numbers. The society's name is printed in several forms (case, 'Limited', 'The'); each form maps to one society, an unknown form is set aside. Organisation_Name can be a person's name: kept as printed, never looked up. No address column. CC BY 4.0 (the catalogue's package page); attribution to Te Tari Taiwhenua Department of Internal Affairs.

config.encoding: utf-8 per field, then Windows-1252, then Latin-1 (counted)
config.dates: day first; a five-digit day number is a spreadsheet date (counted)

process: Parse the CSV as bytes and decode each field on its own.
Every record becomes a grant row or a catch-log line: a record of the wrong width, an unknown society form, no recipient, no year, a year before 2017.
gates: Records counted afresh from the bytes equal the records read (check.py).
on_fail: the whole file set aside, nothing read from it

by: grants-1 session (Opus), step 6.3 (to be appended by the integrator at grants-1)
title: Community Matters: a Lottery committee's record of grants for one round (HTML page)

landmarks: an h1 naming Lottery, a financial year and 'record of grants'
a footnote paragraph after the table starting '*'

signals_note: Recognised by its heading and its table's head, not by its address. Measured on the 2024/25 round two Lottery Community National page (16bd7a0b…, 21 October 2026): 156 rows, amounts '$60,000' with an asterisk on multi-year grants, the footnote '*2 year multi-year grant (no 3 year grants awarded)'. Headings seen by search: year first or last, 'round one'/'round two' before or after the committee, '2024-25' with a hyphen.

tables.one record: one grant the committee made in the round
tables.key: the document's hash and the table row

notes: No purpose, no decision date and no number: the period is the financial year and round in the heading. The Department's page runs a word into 'Incorporated' with no space ('New ZealandIncorporated'); the name is kept as printed. A row named 'Total' is the page's own total, read as a stated figure. CC BY 4.0 per the Community Matters copyright statement (to confirm: the host refused the survey's reading of it); attribution to Te Tari Taiwhenua Department of Internal Affairs.
process: The heading gives the financial year, the round and the committee as printed.
Every table row becomes a grant row, the page's own total, or a catch-log line.
gates: Rows in = grants + catch-log lines (+ a total row).
A stated total, where printed, equals the sum read (check.py).
on_fail: the page set aside, nothing read from it
